candidates.reasoning: Fills the sheer line-out-the-door weekend-breakfast-as-event role better than anything else in Tokyo, with sharing-sized plates and a mostly young crowd treating brunch as a destination. It's the weakest fit on ambition and cooking — Tokyo genuinely lacks a chef-driven brunch institution with multi-generational regulars, since morning eating here is a fast kissaten or hotel affair, so all three candidates are approximations.

candidates.name: Bar Trench
candidates.reasoning: Like Teardrop, Trench is the small, dim room credited with kicking off its city's modern craft-cocktail wave rather than continuing an inherited tradition — house infusions, absinthe obsession, no TVs, and a bar-back lineage that staffed half the good rooms in town. Both are industry pilgrimage stops that still read as a neighborhood bar you can walk into on a Tuesday.

candidates.name: Bar Benfiddich
candidates.reasoning: Nearly as strong an answer: Kayama grows and distills his own herbs and grinds bitters at the bar, which is exactly Teardrop's house-tincture, apothecary-shelf ethos taken to an extreme. It loses a little because it's a singular destination pilgrimage rather than a scene-builder where locals bring an out-of-town colleague.

candidates.name: Bar High Five
candidates.reasoning: The default answer when you want to quietly impress someone — low light, no music of note, a bartender whose stirring people study. It's the more classical, Ginza-tradition version of the role, so it matches Teardrop's seriousness and hospitality but not its scrappy ingredient-tinkering side.

candidates.name: Rock Bar Mother (Koenji)
candidates.reasoning: Koenji is Tokyo's Alberta-to-Sandy-Blvd punk belt, and Mother is the black-walled, flyer-papered rock bar where the same fifteen regulars drink cheap all-nighters and everyone in the room is in or adjacent to a band. Like The Know, it's a bar first and a scene clubhouse second — no cover most nights, no pretension, and the loud records are the decor.

candidates.name: Earthdom (Shin-Okubo)
candidates.reasoning: Nearly as good a fit: a grimy hardcore/punk basement where the bar counter is as much of the hangout as the stage, cheap drinks, and a crowd that treats it as home base rather than a night out. It tips further toward being a venue than The Know does, which is the only reason it isn't first.

candidates.name: Koenji 20000V (Nijuman Denatsu)
candidates.reasoning: The institutional heart of Tokyo punk — decades of local bands, sticky floors, cheap entry, and a name that signals allegiance the way The Know's does in Portland. Weighted more toward legendary-venue status and less toward drop-in drinking, so it captures the identity but not the everyday role.
